subject.summary: Android checkout screen and the first-launch permission flow before it, reviewed from a written description.
evidence: written description of the screen and the first-launch flow

lenses.reason: Primary action and irreversible charge are described.
A countdown scarcity banner is described.
Covered by the usability hierarchy finding; no separate goal question.
Permission timing on first launch is described.

category_health.summary: 1 blocker (irreversible charge, A05R), 1 moderate (equal-weight actions, A01R).

missing_context.text: Color contrast and text scaling are not assessable from a written description.
missing_context.resolves_with: A screenshot and a running build with large text enabled.

missing_context.text: Offline and payment-declined states were not described.

top3.text: Add a review step before the card is charged.
Expand the Place order touch region to 48x48dp.

accessibility/core.md#X03.text: Text meets contrast requirements; WCAG AA baseline is 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for qualifying large text.

accessibility/mobile.md#T02.text: Android interactive touch targets are at least 48x48 dp; visible artwork may be smaller if the focus/touch area is large enough.

psychology/behavioral-economics.md#PB08.text: Scarcity and countdown urgency must reflect a real constraint; resetting timers or fake low-stock claims are deceptive patterns.
psychology/behavioral-economics.md#PB08.sources: NN/g Deceptive Patterns in UX; NN/g The Vortex

trust/mobile.md#O04.text: Do not request all permissions at startup. Request a permission when the user invokes the feature that needs it.
trust/mobile.md#O04.sources: Apple HIG Privacy; Android Request runtime permissions, App permissions best practices; NN/g 3 Design Considerations for Effective Mobile-App Permission Requests

trust/mobile.md#O05.text: Before an unexpected/sensitive permission, explain what is accessed and the user-facing benefit in clear language.
trust/mobile.md#O05.sources: Apple HIG Privacy; Android Request runtime permissions; NN/g Permission Requests

usability/core.md#A01R.text: Each screen has a visually clear primary action when the task has a clear next step; secondary actions receive less emphasis.
usability/core.md#A01R.sources: Apple HIG Buttons; Android Layouts and navigation patterns; Baymard Institute, Holst, "35 Data-Driven Ecommerce Best Practices" (2021: the main add-to-cart control uses a style not used on other buttons)

usability/core.md#A02R.text: Button labels describe the action, preferably with concise verbs; avoid vague labels such as "OK" when a specific action is possible.
usability/core.md#A02R.sources: Apple HIG Buttons, Writing; NN/g Confirmation Dialogs Can Prevent User Errors

usability/core.md#A03R.text: Custom controls have visible pressed/active/disabled/selected states so interaction never feels ambiguous.
usability/core.md#A03R.sources: Apple HIG Buttons, Feedback; NN/g Ten Usability Heuristics

usability/core.md#A04R.text: Routine reversible destructive actions prefer Undo/recovery over repetitive confirmation dialogs.
usability/core.md#A04R.sources: Apple HIG Alerts; NN/g Confirmation Dialogs, Using Swipe to Trigger Contextual Actions; Android Snackbar; Don Norman, *The Design of Everyday Things* (Revised and Expanded Edition, Basic Books, 2013), Chapter 5 (make actions reversible)

usability/core.md#A05R.text: Irreversible/high-cost destructive actions use a specific confirmation that explains the consequence and names the object/action.
usability/core.md#A05R.sources: Apple HIG Alerts, Action sheets; NN/g Confirmation Dialogs

findings.title: Place order hit area is 30x30dp
findings.observation: The Place order control is 30x30dp on Android, with a small icon and no label text.
findings.why_it_matters: Missed and accidental taps on the main conversion action, worst for people with motor impairments.
findings.recommendation: Keep the icon and expand the touch region to at least 48x48dp.
false_positive_conditions: 30x30dp is only the artwork and the touch region is already at least 48x48dp.
validation_method: Measure the touch region with the Android layout inspector.

options.text: Keep the icon and expand the touch region to at least 48x48dp. One layout change; the screen looks the same.
Replace the icon with a full-width labeled "Place order" button. A larger visual change that also adds the missing label.

picture.caption: The solid square is the 30dp control; the dashed square is the 48dp minimum touch region.

panels.html: 48 x 48 dp

findings.title: Place order charges the card with no confirmation or undo
findings.observation: Tapping Place order charges the card at once. There is no confirmation step and no undo.
findings.why_it_matters: An accidental tap is an unrecoverable payment.
findings.recommendation: Show a review step that names the amount and the card, with a "Pay $42.00" button.
false_positive_conditions: The order can be cancelled free of charge for some minutes after placing it, and the screen says so.
validation_method: Place a test order on a staging build and check for a confirmation or cancel window.

options.text: Add a review step that names the amount and the card, with a "Pay $42.00" button. One extra screen in the flow.
Keep one tap, and add a free cancel window of 5 minutes with a visible "Cancel order" control. Needs back-end support for cancellation.

findings.title: All permissions are requested at first launch
findings.observation: On first launch the app asks for location, camera and notifications together, before any feature needs them.
findings.why_it_matters: People deny permissions they cannot connect to a benefit, and many never grant them later.
findings.recommendation: Ask for each permission when the person first uses the feature that needs it, after a one-line benefit explanation.
false_positive_conditions: The first screen of the app is a feature that needs all three permissions at once.
validation_method: Record a first launch on a clean install and list each permission prompt with the screen that caused it.

options.text: Ask for each permission in context, when its feature is first used, after a one-line benefit explanation. Moves three prompts into three features.

picture.caption: Before: three prompts on launch. After: each prompt waits for its feature.

findings.title: Stock countdown resets on every reload
findings.observation: The banner "Only 2 left in stock — order in the next 10 minutes!" restarts its countdown each time the screen reloads.
findings.why_it_matters: A timer that restarts is fabricated urgency: a deceptive pattern that costs trust once noticed.
findings.recommendation: Remove the countdown; show stock only when it comes from real inventory data.
false_positive_conditions: The countdown is tied to a real reservation that expires, and the stock count is live.
validation_method: Reload the screen twice and compare the timer; compare the stock count with the inventory API.

options.text: Remove the countdown and show stock only from live inventory. Removes one banner.
Tie the timer to a real cart reservation that expires once and say so ("Reserved for 10 min"). Needs a reservation back end.

findings.title: Place order and Save for later have equal weight
findings.observation: Place order and Save for later sit side by side with the same size and color.
findings.why_it_matters: The primary action does not stand out, so people hesitate or tap the wrong one.
findings.recommendation: Make Place order the single filled primary button; show Save for later as a text or outline button.
false_positive_conditions: Saving for later is the main goal of this screen for most people.
validation_method: Run a five-second test asking which button completes the purchase.

options.text: Make Place order the single filled button and Save for later an outline button. Style change only.
